claims.text_en: BTS Saphan Khwai (N7) is an elevated Sukhumvit Line station opened 5 December 1999 on Phahonyothin Road at the Saphan Khwai intersection in Phaya Thai district (13.7938 N, 100.54973 E per the article; OSM node 13.79382, 100.54971), between Ari and Mo Chit, with 1,427,958 passengers in 2021. The station fronts Saphan Khwai market and Paolo Memorial Hospital, with a Big C supercenter and the Thai Philatelic Museum at the Sam Sen Nai post office to the south. The encyclopedic article carrying these facts is a flagged unsourced stub.

geography.notes: App anchor 13.7914 sits ~270 m south of the OSM node — reconcile with unit centroid convention.

evidence.paraphrase: N7, opened 5 Dec 1999, Phahonyothin Rd at Saphan Khwai intersection, Phaya Thai district, coords, 2021 ridership 1,427,958, in front of Saphan Khwai market and Paolo Memorial Hospital; Big C and Philatelic Museum south.
OSM station node tagged Saphan Khwai N7 at 13.79382/100.54971, operator BTSC.

limitations: Underlying article is unsourced; ridership figure not corroborated by a second read source.

claims.text_en: Naming and scope: the BTS signage spells 'Saphan Khwai' while the neighbourhood commonly writes 'Saphan Kwai' — the same place; the neighbourhood is described as sitting on the Phaya Thai / Chatuchak border, defined by Phahonyothin Road, with a west side (dense Pradiphat Road band and market approaches) and a thinner residential east side beyond the railway.

geography.notes: Khet split (Phaya Thai vs Chatuchak) inside one unit is plausible given the border position; polygon decides.

evidence.paraphrase: Signage romanization differs from neighbourhood spelling; station straddles the road; west side dense Pradiphat band, east side thinner residential beyond the railway; described as Phaya Thai/Chatuchak border (site index).

claims.text_en: Walkability is real but directional: of 529 places in the neighbourhood dataset, 373 fall within 800 m straight-line of the station (the site treats that band as the walkable core, which it equates to roughly a 10-12 minute walk) and 60 within 400 m; but Phahonyothin Road's spaced crossings mean a place 150 m away across the road can take longer to reach than one 400 m on the same side — the site's rule is 'check which side of Phahonyothin you want before you set off'. All distances are straight-line; the site warns real walks are always longer.

geography.notes: The 10-12 minute equivalence is the source's own reported figure, not an agent conversion.

evidence.paraphrase: 373 of 529 within 800 m, 60 within 400 m; 800 m treated as walkable core; crossing constraint quote; straight-line caveat.

limitations: Counts cover food/drink/personal-services places, not all amenities (the site says services categories are too thin to count honestly).

claims.text_en: The corridor's defining downside is the road itself: a wide, fast, multi-lane artery whose BTS viaduct shades most of it and makes it noisy, with no centre — the site calls the station 'an intersection, not a square'. A major north-south bus corridor parallels the BTS ('much cheaper and much slower'), and motorbike-taxi ranks at soi mouths cover the awkward middle distance.

evidence.paraphrase: Big multi-lane road, fast traffic, viaduct shade and noise, spaced crossings; bus corridor cheaper/slower; motorbike ranks standard for middle distances.
Phahonyothin 'wide, fast and constant'; no centre — 'an intersection, not a square'.

claims.text_en: Food is the unit's engine: the neighbourhood dataset holds 175 restaurants and 149 coffee shops/cafés among its 529 places; Pradiphat Road west of the station is called 'the food spine — the densest run of small kitchens in the neighbourhood'; and the Aqua pedestrian courtyard between Phahonyothin Sois 14-16 clusters restaurants and cafés (Filete, Smiley Shrimp, Yakizen, Ansel & Elliott per the travel guide). At the unit's north-west edge sits Or Tor Kor market — described as Thailand's best-known fresh market, daily, covered, partly air-conditioned, premium-priced rather than cheap.

geography.notes: Aqua courtyard (Sois 14-16) is south of the station node toward Ari — likely inside or at the unit's edge; OTK at the NW edge straddles the Kamphaeng Phet unit boundary.

evidence.paraphrase: 175 restaurants, 149 coffee shops/cafés of 529 places; sub-area breakdown Chatuchak Market 208, Pradiphat Road 80, station core 56, Or Tor Kor 49.

evidence.locator: Pradiphat framing on index; 'Eating on Pradiphat Road' description
evidence.paraphrase: Pradiphat Road as food spine.
Most restaurants cluster in Aqua courtyard between Sois 14-16; named venues listed.
OTK graded/curated premium fresh market, daily, covered, partly air-conditioned, expensive by fresh-market standards.

limitations: Dataset excludes most services and vendors inside markets; venue longevity not verified.

claims.text_en: Nightlife is denser than the 'gritty' label suggests but stays local-scale: 49 bars/pubs sit inside the 1.2 km dataset boundary, 39 of them open past 9 pm as of 2 August 2026 — closest AV Izakaya 128 m from the station (closes 1 am), Old Dirty in the south fringe 604 m away closing 2 am, with several 2 am venues (Honest Mistake Bar, Glur.bar, MOMO BAR). The travel guide's counter-view: it is 'not the city's best for nightlife', with gastropubs (Old Dirty live music, Brewix) plus a low-price, Thai-oriented go-go strip on Sutthisan Winitchai Road — a bar-hopping neighbourhood rather than a party district.

geography.notes: Counts use a 1.2 km site boundary wider than the 800 m catchment; several venues (south fringe, Pradiphat far end) may fall outside the unit polygon.

evidence.paraphrase: 49 bars/pubs in boundary, 39 open at/after 9 pm; AV Izakaya 128 m closes 1 am; Old Dirty 604 m closes 2 am; straight-line caveat; ratings are a weak signal.
Not the city's best for nightlife; gastropubs Old Dirty and Brewix; Sutthisan Winitchai Rd go-go strip with low prices, little English.

limitations: The app's 15 nightlife venues cannot be reconciled to the site's 49-bar boundary figure without the polygon; venue hours change often per the source.

claims.text_en: Rents match the unit's value positioning: HipFlat's Phaya Thai district averages (2,253 condo listings, October data) run USD 474 studio / USD 652 one-bedroom / USD 1,037 two-bedroom, while THB-denominated listings near this station go lower — M Jatujak (Soi Phahonyothin 18, ~400 m to BTS Saphan Khwai) at 18,000-19,000 baht for 29-33 sqm one-beds, Vela De Residence 12,000 baht (24 sqm), Rhythm Phahol-Ari 18,000-23,000 baht. A May 2026 expat guide puts studio/one-bed starts at 12,000-18,000 baht and newer-pool-gym one-beds at 15,000-22,000, two-beds 25,000-40,000. The app's 18,000/36,500 Phaya Thai blend sits inside these ranges.

geography.notes: District-wide proxy includes pricier Ari/Sanam Pao; station-adjacent THB listings are the better anchor.

evidence.locator: 'Average price by bedrooms' + listings near Saphan Khwai
evidence.paraphrase: Studio USD474 / 1BR USD652 / 2BR USD1,037; M Jatujak ฿18,000-19,000; Vela De ฿12,000; Rhythm Phahol-Ari ฿18,000-23,000.
Studio/1BR 12,000-18,000 start; newer 1BR 15,000-22,000; 2BR 25,000-40,000; example lease 16,000 at Ideo Q Phaya Thai.

limitations: HipFlat averages in USD without stated conversion; Superagent is content-marketing with anecdotal figures.

claims.text_en: Green is the unit's weakest card and the app's green 6 looks generous against the evidence: the neighbourhood guide states there is 'almost no green space; Chatuchak Park is a trip, not a stroll', and the Overpass search found no leisure=park centroid within 850 m of the station node — only condominium gardens and two small dog parks toward the Kamphaeng Phet side. The app maps just 0.7 ha of park inside the unit.

geography.notes: App's 0.7 ha mapped park has no named OSM counterpart in the search band — verify which parcel it is.

evidence.paraphrase: Almost no green space; Chatuchak Park 'a trip, not a stroll'.
Only unnamed condo leisure=garden ways and two dog parks near the Kamphaeng Phet side; no named public park centroid within 850 m.

limitations: OSM completeness for small pocket parks is imperfect; a 0.7 ha parcel could exist untagged or tagged differently.

claims.text_en: Daily rhythm runs early and closes earlier than areas to the south: 51 of 445 places with published hours open before 7 am (concentrated around the markets), 163 still trade at 9 pm, 374 open Sundays, and the guide notes the neighbourhood 'closes earlier than Ari and southern areas'; BTS stops before midnight, so the 81 places open at 11 pm are reached by taxi or motorbike taxi, not rail.

evidence.paraphrase: 445 places with hours; 374 open Sundays; 51 before 7 am; 163 open at 9 pm; closes earlier than Ari and southern areas.
81 places open at 11pm; post-train travel means taxi/ride-hail.

limitations: Hours are business-listing data that the source says change often.

claims.text_en: Crowding is moderate by north-Bangkok standards and the transport experience is livable at peak: the guide says you can board trains in the morning rush here 'unlike further south', and the station's 2021 ridership (1.43 million) is roughly a quarter of Mo Chit's (5.17 million) a stop north — consistent with a busy local corridor rather than a hub crush. No source quantifies street-level crowding for this unit specifically.

geography.notes: App crowd 3 has no unit-specific measurement behind it in any read source.

evidence.paraphrase: Boardable trains in morning rush, unlike further south.
1,427,958 passengers in 2021 (vs Mo Chit BTS 5,166,915 per the Mo Chit article read for the sibling unit).

limitations: 2021 ridership reflects COVID-era levels; relative ranking more meaningful than absolutes.

claims.text_en: Gentrification is the observed 2020s trend and the honest gaps are safety and recent change: the travel guide describes a neighbourhood 'gentrifying quickly' but still 'gritty, industrial', with craft-beer bars arriving among old shophouses and a hostel cluster (Everyday Sunday, Adventure Hostel by the BTS, KENCOZY, Buff), and the neighbourhood guide's verdict is to live in a soi off western Pradiphat Road with the quietest pocket east of the railway on Saliratthawiphak. No read source addresses crime or safety for this unit (app safety 8 is unverified), and no 2024-2026 construction or opening was found in read sources — the strongest dated signal is the guide dataset's August 2026 snapshot.

evidence.paraphrase: Gentrifying quickly, gritty industrial feel, craft beer bars among old shophouses, best hostels, few tourist attractions.
Live in a soi off western Pradiphat; quietest is Saliratthawiphak east of the railway.

limitations: Safety 8 unverified — no crime data or resident reports accessible (Reddit/TripAdvisor 403 per brief); travel guide undated.

preview.text_en: One BTS stop south of the market and one north of Ari: a fast, viaduct-shaded stretch of Phahonyothin where 175 restaurants and 149 cafés pack the sois, 39 bars trade past 9 pm, and a one-bed at M Jatujak rents for 18,000 baht — with almost no green space and streets that close earlier than the neighbourhoods to the south.

guide_lead.text_en: Saphan Khwai is the working corridor between Ari's cafe rows and the Chatuchak market edge: BTS N7 over a wide, fast Phahonyothin Road, Pradiphat Road as the dense food spine, Or Tor Kor market at the unit's north-west corner, and 39 bars still pouring past 9 pm. Rents run below the app's Phaya Thai blend at station-adjacent buildings (12,000-23,000 baht studios and one-beds captured), while the two-bed blend of 36,500 matches district ranges. The frictions: 'almost no green space' by the neighbourhood guide's own account, a road you can only cross at spaced points, early closing by southern-Bangkok standards, and a safety score with no unit-specific evidence behind it.

strengths.text_en: Density of everyday food and drink: 175 restaurants and 149 cafés in the neighbourhood dataset, a named food spine on Pradiphat Road, and premium daily shopping at Or Tor Kor at the unit's edge.
Value rents with boardable rush-hour trains: station-adjacent one-beds captured at 12,000-23,000 baht, below the district blend, and morning trains you can actually board.

tradeoffs.text_en: The road dominates: wide, fast, viaduct-noisy, crossable only at spaced points, with no centre — 'an intersection, not a square'.
Green and late hours are thin: 'almost no green space' (Chatuchak Park 'a trip, not a stroll'), closing earlier than Ari, and no park centroid within 850 m in OSM.

day_night.text_en: Mornings start before 7 am around the markets; evenings wind down by Ari's standards — 163 of 445 timed places still open at 9 pm, 39 bars past 9 pm, and post-midnight movement by taxi or motorbike taxi once BTS stops.

within_area_variation.text_en: The west side (Pradiphat band, market approaches) carries the density; the east side beyond the railway is the quiet residential pocket (Saliratthawiphak), and the south fringe toward Ari holds most of the 2 am bars.

conditional_fit.text_en: Fit for value-seeking renters and food-first residents who accept road noise and early closing; the hostels and craft-beer arrivals suit a young, mobile crowd.
Poor fit for green-space daily users and late-night rail commuters — the park is a trip, not a stroll, and the BTS stops before the last bars do.

uncertainties: Nightlife count basis: app 15 venues vs the neighbourhood dataset's 49 bars in a wider 1.2 km boundary — polygon decides (saphan-khwai-c06).
The app's 0.7 ha mapped park has no identified OSM counterpart; green 6 may be generous (saphan-khwai-c08).
